title: Routine prenatal visits
what: Regular doctor visits during pregnancy. The doctor checks your health and your baby's growth.
why: For all pregnant women, on a schedule: less often at first, more often closer to the birth.
duration: the visit usually takes 15 to 30 minutes
tell_doctor: How you feel and what bothers you
Swelling, headaches, or spots before your eyes
How your baby is moving, in the second half of pregnancy
Any new medicines you have started

prepare.title: Urine sample
prepare.text: A urine test is often needed at each visit. Collect your first morning urine in a clean container.

prepare.title: Questions
prepare.text: Write down questions between visits so you do not forget.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something comfortable that lets you uncover your belly easily.

bring: A urine sample, if you were asked
steps: You are weighed, and your blood pressure is checked
The doctor asks how you feel
Your belly is measured with a tape measure
In the second half of pregnancy, the doctor listens to your baby's heartbeat
Your test results are reviewed, and new tests are ordered
The date of your next visit is set
feel: A pelvic exam is not done at every visit
after: Have your tests and ultrasounds on schedule
Keep notes on how you feel and how your baby moves
Come on the set day, even if everything is fine
red_flags: Bleeding or leaking fluid: call emergency services
A severe headache, spots before your eyes, or sudden swelling: call emergency services
Your baby is moving much less than usual: see a doctor urgently
Contractions before your due time: call emergency services

faq.q: How often do I need to see the doctor?
faq.a: Usually once a month at first, every 2 weeks in the second half, and every week at the end. Your doctor will tell you.

faq.q: Why a urine test every time?
faq.a: It catches protein, sugar, and infection early. This matters for you and your baby.

reminders.text: Prenatal visit tomorrow. Bring your pregnancy record, and collect a morning urine sample if you were asked.
